newsitem.title: UK: Firstbus confirms has Gt Eastern rail deal.
newsitem.headline: Firstbus confirms has Gt Eastern rail deal.

text.p: British passenger transport company Firstbus Plc confirmed on Wednesday that it had been awarded a seven-year franchise to run the Great Eastern passenger rail operating company under Britain's privatisation plan.
Over the life of the franchise, the company will see its financial support of 29.0 million stg in the first year switch to a premium payment of 9.5 million stg in 2004.
"This represents average support of 5.6 million stg per annum," the company said in a statement, which confirmed an earlier story carried by the Press Association new agency.
Great Eastern runs services, mainly based on commuter traffic, between London's Liverpool Street station and the suburbs and counties to the east and northeast of the city.
Trevor Smallwood, Firstbus chairman, said the company already knew the region well and was keen to exploit the potential for links between bus and rail.
Part of the contract with the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising will include Firstbus spending over 9.0 million stg on improved stations, including lighting and security upgrades.
Firstbus shares rose during Wednesday morning to stand up 4-1/2 pence at 198-1/2 pence by 1040 GMT.
